## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-general`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-general)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-general`:

$$
2^{O(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(n(\log\log n)^2/\sqrt{\log n})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Keep all declared vertices. Enumerate directed triangles in O(n^3) time. The empty tournament contributes one empty deletion set. Handle a requested size outside [0,n] with count zero.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(n)$ |
| Clauses | $O(n^3+n)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. A tournament has a directed cycle if and only if it has a directed triangle. Indeed, if a shortest directed cycle had length at least four, the arc between its first and third vertices would give either a directed triangle or a shorter directed cycle. Vertex deletion preserves the tournament property.

2. Therefore D is a feedback vertex set exactly when it hits every directed triangle. Put one deletion bit x_v per vertex and a clause $x_a\vee x_b\vee x_c$ for each directed triangle on a,b,c. The triangle-hitting formulation is also stated in the cited source; this entry does not use its kernel theorem.

3. Each original deletion set has exactly one assignment to these bits. For cardinality t add $\sum_v x_v=t$ using the full-equivalence linear-size circuit. Including all gate outputs gives N=O(n), M=O(n^3+n), and width at most three, with a unique extension for each eligible set.

4. The encoded bit length is O((n^3+n) log(n+2)). Apply the general-density exact-counting assumption to get A(n)L^{O(1)} time and polynomial space. Despite the input tournament being dense, its arcs and triangles contribute clauses rather than additional selection variables.

5. Running the size-refined count for t=0,...,n gives the full size distribution with polynomial overhead. Its first positive entry counts optimum feedback vertex sets; comparing that number with one decides optimum uniqueness. A separate optimization entry provides an optimum witness.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- This is an exact algorithm measured in the original vertex count n. It does not establish a subexponential FPT bound in the deletion budget k; that separate transfer remains a candidate.
- Do not use a decision kernel when counting without checking its multiplicities. Retaining every original vertex ensures that even vertices in no triangle are counted correctly.
- The triangle argument is for vertex deletion in tournaments. In a general digraph, a directed cycle need not contain a triangle; deleting arcs from a tournament can also leave a directed cycle without a triangle.
- No weighted, inclusion-minimal-counting, or full-enumeration running-time claim is made.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
